title: All-powerful, all-loving
hook: classic attributes: God is almighty, all-knowing, everywhere, and love

segments.voice: Yesterday, apophatic: speaking of God by what God is not. Your line was more than you think. Who got a quiet not quite from you? Day one thousand sixty-nine.

"I believe in God the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth." In churches that say the Apostles' Creed, a whole room says that line together, out loud, some of them half awake, some of them meaning every word. Almighty is one of the first things it says about God. Yesterday was the way of not: what God is not. Today goes the other way, to the old list of what Christians say God is. Almighty, all-knowing, everywhere, and love. Four words. Put the first one next to the last one, and things get interesting. Today's word: all-powerful.
screen: `FROM WHAT GOD IS NOT, TO WHAT GOD IS.`

segments.voice: Christian teachers have long spoken of God's attributes, the things that are true of God. Four of them are on today's list. All-powerful: in Genesis, God says to Abram, "I am the Almighty God; walk before me, and be thou perfect." All-knowing and everywhere: these come alive in Psalm 139, and the psalm doesn't sound like a textbook. It sounds like someone who can't get away. "For there is not a word in my tongue, but, lo, O LORD, thou knowest it altogether." Then: "Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence?" Heaven, the grave, the far side of the sea: God is there too. And at the far side of the sea, the psalm turns: "Even there shall thy hand lead me, and thy right hand shall hold me." Being known everywhere stops being surveillance and becomes being held. Then the fourth word. The first letter of John says it plainly: "He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love." Notice the grammar. The Bible calls God almighty, but in this letter love is not just something God has or does. It's what God is. Some teachers read the whole list through that line: power that serves love, knowledge that loves what it knows, a presence that holds. And honesty matters here. Put all-powerful beside all-loving, then look at a hospital ward or a news feed, and hard questions appear. Christians have wrestled with them for a long time, and do still. The list doesn't answer every question. It tells you which word some Christians put first.

Here's the practice: walk through the four words, and notice which one meets you. Settle, and breathe. On one breath: almighty. On the next: all-knowing. Then: everywhere. Then: love. Go round again, slowly. Notice which one you lean toward today, and whether any of them unsettles you. Both are worth noticing. You don't have to explain why. If you pray, you can rest on the word that met you, and stay with it until the bell. The bell holds the time.
All-powerful. Almighty, as the creed says, and in the first letter of John, held together with the line God is love.
Your line: god is love first. Today, if you have any power over anything, a team, a kid, a decision, use one bit of it for someone else's good. Day one thousand sixty-nine.

howItsDone: In churches that use the Apostles' or Nicene Creed, congregations confess God as the Father Almighty, and preaching and hymns often pair God's power with God's love, drawing on Psalm 139 and the first letter of John.

original.note: Greek: the Almighty, ruler of all; a title for God in the creeds and in Revelation.

trapdoor: what you thought: all-powerful means God can do whatever, whenever.
what it means: one of four classic words, almighty, all-knowing, everywhere and love, and some Christians read the first three through the last.
what a scholar hears: 1 John says God is love, at 4:8 and again at 4:16. the letter never says God is power. it says God is love, and some readers build on that.

notes: 'Four of them are on today's list' counts the outline's list (almighty, all-knowing, everywhere, love), not all classical attributes. Confirm wording.
Apostles' Creed quoted from the BCP 1662 wording; please verify against the 1662 text.
'Christian teachers have long spoken of God's attributes' and 'Christians have wrestled with them for a long time' are soft time claims with no number. Confirm.

Trapdoor: 1 John 'God is love' at 4:8 and 4:16 is stated from the text itself. 'Power is something God has; love is what God is' is an interpretive reading; attributed to 'some Christians' in the teach. Confirm.
Original: παντοκράτωρ (Pantokrator), the Greek behind 'Almighty' in the Nicene Creed and Revelation (e.g. 1:8). Confirm.
The problem of suffering is named but not taught, to leave room for later days in Block A. Index hook kept verbatim.

Audit: trapdoor's third floor stated an interpretation ('power is something God has; love is what God is') as a scholar's fact; now says only what the letter says and attributes the reading to some readers.
